transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-15
Time: 14:00 PT
Duration: ~45m
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Daniel Ortiz (HarborTrust TPM), Maria Gonzales (Infra Lead), Tom Reed (Eng Manager)

[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I think we have about 45 minutes. Quick agenda: TTFT numbers, streaming behavior, kernel choices, and next steps. Priya will run through the numbers.
[00:18] Priya: yeah hi, okay so last run we did on the dedicated test pool, we saw TTFT at about 220ms median for short prompts, um but as context jumps to 8k it climbs to about 420ms, there's some variance. We used the default kernel selection, and quantized weights to int8.
[00:37] Daniel: sorry can I stop you - when you say TTFT 220ms is that cold start or warm?
[00:41] Priya: warm, warm cache for the model, so KV cache was primed. Cold starts were higher, in the 600 to 800ms range on our infra.
[00:51] Tom: okay that's a bit higher than we hoped - our SLO is 150ms for interactive flows.
[00:56] Alex: yeah right, so we need to focus on two levers: streaming (so we get first token out earlier) and kernel choices + batch sizing to reduce latency. Also prefix caching behavior - if you have repeated prefixes we can shave a lot.
[01:10] Maria: quick question, when you say streaming flush interval, do you mean the chunk size in tokens or time-based flush?
[01:16] Priya: good call - it's currently token-chunked at 32 tokens with a 50ms flush fallback, so it's hybrid. For short outputs we sometimes wait until the 32 token chunk fills which adds 30-50ms.
[01:29] Daniel: hmm, in our real traces most responses are 8-24 tokens final, so chunking at 32 is actually hurting us.
[01:36] Priya: yeah that's the thing - we recommended trying smaller chunks (8 or 12) for your workload, but there's a CPU overhead per chunk. Tradeoff between more frequent flushes and CPU scheduling.
[01:48] Alex: also kernel selection - the runtime picked the generic attention kernel for the 8k context path, but there's a faster fused kernel for decoder-only models at medium sequence lengths; schedule wise it didn't trigger because of sequence shape. If we force a different kernel it might change latency.
[02:03] Priya: to add, quantization also affects kernel choice; int8 has different optimal kernels than fp16.
[02:10] Tom: is that safe for quality? our compliance team is sensitive to hallucinations.
[02:15] Priya: in our evals we saw negligible quality delta for int8 on your prompt sets, but we'll run targeted evals. We'll include the eval pass as part of the microbenchmarks.
[02:26] Daniel: regarding KV cache, we noticed a thing where repeated system prompts still re-evaluate for some requests, unclear if the prefix cache is being hit on your test harness.
[02:35] Priya: uh huh, that's likely the prefix normalization on your side - or the request metadata is changing (conversation ids). We'll instrument with headers to confirm cache hits.
[02:43] Maria: for Private deployment testing, networking will matter - when the control plane talks to your on-prem runtime we need to know expected outbound ports and KMS calls frequency.
[02:53] Alex: yep, we'll share the network and KMS doc. Maria, we should set a follow-up for the infra deep-dive.
[02:58] Daniel: one more thing - competitor note: we ran a quick bench with Bedrock and saw lower median TTFT for small contexts but higher variance on long contexts. just FYI.
[03:08] Priya: thanks. For today's action plan I propose: run TTFT microbenchmarks across seq 128/256/512 and target kernel overrides, test streaming chunk sizes 8/12/16, and capture CPU utilization. We'll also test cold start improvements with pre-warming.
[03:25] Alex: sounds good. On pre-warming, we can use small persistent pools or keepalive to reduce cold starts; there's a cost tradeoff. We'll include cost estimates in the spreadsheet.
[03:34] Tom: any quick wins for us to try before next week?
[03:36] Priya: switch streaming chunk to 12 and reduce flush to 30ms - you should see TTFT drop ~30 to 50ms for short responses. Also enable prefix caching for system messages - if you have stable prompts that saves us cycles.
[03:48] Daniel: okay we'll try the streaming tweak in staging tomorrow.
[03:51] Maria: I'll extract our request traces and topology and share by Friday.
[03:55] Alex: I'll send the perf spreadsheet and security docs after this call. Priya will push the microbenchmark results mid-next-week.
[04:02] [brief crosstalk]
[04:08] Priya: tiny note - we saw one outlier where kernel fell back to a slower matmul implementation due to alignment, that can happen with certain sequence shapes, we'll include a kernel selection log in the report.
[04:19] Tom: can you also include the per-token cost impact if we change to smaller chunks? we need cost numbers for SRE.
[04:25] Alex: yes, cost delta will be in the sheet (estimated token CPU cost + persistent pool run rate).
[04:30] Daniel: ok recap?
[04:32] Alex: recap: Priya runs microbenchmarks (TTFT, kernel overrides, streaming chunk sizes), Maria shares infra/network info + request traces, Alex sends perf/security docs and cost estimates, schedule infra deep-dive next week. Next meeting same time next Tuesday unless we adjust.
[04:48] Tom: thanks everyone.
[04:50] Alex: thanks, bye.

Notes: Some transcription artifacts present ("K V cash" for KV cache in raw auto-transcript), proper nouns occasionally misspelled (Bedrock noted as "Bed rock" in transcript), speaker labels approximate. Links shared: perf spreadsheet (link posted in chat), security one-pager (SOC2 summary).
